Why Oracle fired 30000 employees ? AI Bubble explained #ai #oracle #layoffs

Behind the headlines of Oracle’s recent record-breaking cloud contracts lies a much colder reality for its workforce. As of April 2026, the company has confirmed a massive layoff of 30,000 employees—nearly 20% of its global staff—driven by a high-stakes pivot toward the "Stargate" AI supercomputing project with OpenAI. While Oracle's revenue is technically growing, the company is caught in a precarious "capital shuffle": it is taking on billions in debt to buy Nvidia chips and build data centers, essentially trading human payroll for raw processing power. With the stock sliding nearly 25% this year and interest rates making that debt increasingly expensive, leadership is gutting traditional software roles to self-fund a multi-billion dollar bet on an AI future. It’s a move that critics are calling a "circular bubble," where investor money flows from OpenAI to Oracle and back to Nvidia, leaving thousands of veteran engineers behind in the pursuit of silicon-based intelligence.

Market Crash Signs for 2026 | Business | Sarthak Ahuja

The world today is showing 3 signs that are very similar to what happened exactly before the Great Depression in 1929, and the Dot Com Bubble in the year 2000...

👉🏼 First, the stock market valuation multiples... in the Cyclically Adjusted Price to Earnings (CAPE) Ratio or the Shiller PE Ratio...

This ratio looks at the market cap or value of a company divided by the past ten years average earnings after adjusting for inflation.

It provides a smoother, long term view of valuations... and looks at whether stocks are overvalued or undervalued from a long term market cycle perspective.

This ratio was above 32 in 1929... had again crossed 32 in the year 2000... and is currently at 39, which seems absolutely obnoxious...

👉🏼 The second big factor is the concentration of valuation of the market index or the S&P 500 among a few companies...

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced a flurry of new partnerships and dismissed concerns about an AI bubble. 

The company is teaming up with Uber Technologies Inc., Palantir Technologies Inc. and CrowdStrike Holdings Inc., among others, to ensure its technology remains at the heart of the AI frenzy.

Huang emphasized that artificial intelligence models are now powerful enough that customers are willing to pay for them, which will justify the costly build-out of computing infrastructure and ease fears of an AI investment bubble.
